Carbon Credit Eligibility
Factory Reports & Carbon Opportunities

Know what the report is for — and what business decision it supports.

Factories do not need every report for the same reason. Some measure the company, some measure the product, some support exports or disclosure, and some identify projects that may later qualify for carbon credits.

Important: a carbon report does not automatically create carbon credits. Reports build the emissions evidence, baseline and reduction picture. A separate carbon-credit eligibility assessment is then needed to test methodology fit, additionality, MRV, ownership, scale and project economics.

Carbon Credit Eligibility Assessment

Credit Screen
What it tests

Whether a proposed factory intervention has a credible carbon-credit pathway: eligible activity, applicable methodology, baseline, additionality, ownership, monitoring capability, expected volume and project economics.

Why a factory needs it

It prevents the factory from spending on registration or verification before knowing whether the project is technically and commercially realistic as a carbon-credit project.

Decision visualSchematic — not a credit guarantee

Corporate GHG Inventory

GHG / ISO 14064-1
What it measures

Annual emissions from the factory and organisation, including direct fuel/process emissions, purchased electricity and relevant value-chain sources.

Why a factory needs it

It establishes the factory's carbon baseline, identifies major emission sources and supports targets, customer requests, ESG reporting and internal reduction planning.

GHG / ISO 14064-1Sources → baseline → priorities

Decarbonisation Roadmap

Action Plan
What it produces

A prioritised plan of reduction measures such as energy efficiency, process changes, renewable energy, material substitution, waste reduction or technology upgrades.

Why a factory needs it

It translates carbon data into investment decisions by showing what to do first, expected emissions impact, data needs and where deeper engineering or financial analysis is required.

Action roadmapSequence, not a forecast

Waste & Material Flow Assessment

Efficiency
What it measures

Where raw materials, by-products, rejects, packaging, waste and resource losses occur across the production process — ideally linked to cost and emissions.

Why a factory needs it

It can uncover operational savings before large capital investment, improve resource efficiency and create a prioritised list of waste-reduction and circular-economy actions.

Flow diagramShows where value can leak

Product Carbon Footprint

ISO 14067
What it measures

The greenhouse-gas footprint of a specific product or unit across a defined life-cycle boundary, expressed as CO₂e per product, tonne, m³ or other functional unit.

Why a factory needs it

Useful when buyers, export markets or procurement teams want product-level carbon data, and when the factory wants to compare materials, energy options or production scenarios.

ISO 14067One product, defined boundary

CBAM Readiness

EU Export
What it measures

The embedded emissions and supporting production data needed for products that fall within the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism scope.

Why a factory needs it

For relevant EU-facing exports, it helps the factory prepare reliable emissions data for its importer or reporting chain and understand which production steps drive the product's embedded carbon.

Export readinessFactory data → importer disclosure

ESG & Climate Reporting

Disclosure
What it reports

Environmental and climate performance, emissions, targets, risks, governance, policies and selected performance indicators for stakeholders.

Why a factory needs it

It helps answer information requests from boards, banks, investors, customers and supply chains, and turns environmental work into a structured management and disclosure process.

Management viewKPIs + risk + governance

LCA / EPD

ISO 14040/44 • 14025
What it measures

Life Cycle Assessment evaluates environmental impacts across a product's life cycle. An EPD communicates verified environmental results in a standardised product declaration.

Why a factory needs it

Often useful for construction materials, procurement, export tenders and eco-design because it shows where impacts occur beyond the factory gate, not only direct emissions.

ISO 14040/44 • 14025Lifecycle → declaration
From Reporting to Carbon Credits

Measure first. Identify the reduction. Then test credit eligibility.

This separation keeps the factory's reporting credible and avoids promising credits before methodology and additionality are proven.
